next.reason: 1985: reference modification creates a unique data item; leftmost-character-position 'must result in a positive nonzero integer less than or equal to the number of characters', length 'must result in a positive nonzero integer', their sum minus one within the item, and an omitted length extends to the rightmost character (§1985:IV.4.3.8.3.4 GR4). 2023 states the same (§2023:8.4.3.3.4 GR5) except that length 'shall result in a positive nonzero integer, unless the REF-MOD-ZERO-LENGTH directive is set to ON'; with the directive omitted or off a zero length raises EC-BOUND-REF-MOD (§2023:7.3.23.3 GR1). Compiler directives and bit-usage items do not exist in 1985, and the EC-BOUND-REF-MOD sentence reports a violation of a requirement a conforming 1985 program already meets (the 1985 rule is a general rule, not a refusal). A 1985 program means the same.
